heading: Practice
replaces: An unmapped transfer object may only have `AGGREGATION` relations, enforced by the validator ([advanced modeling patterns](../../agent-docs/model/advanced-modeling-patterns.md), *Relation kinds per layer and the bidirectional rules*). The CLI cannot set `AGGREGATION`; it is the default on an unmapped transfer object's transient relation, or the modeling tool sets it.
proposed: An unmapped transfer object may only have `AGGREGATION` relations, enforced by the validator ([advanced modeling patterns](../../agent-docs/model/advanced-modeling-patterns.md), *Relation kinds per layer and the bidirectional rules*). `AGGREGATION` is the default for a transient relation on an unmapped transfer object; the CLI also accepts it explicitly (`create -t OneWayRelationMember --ns <Package>::<TO> -n <rel> -s memberType=TRANSIENT -s relationKind=AGGREGATION`), and `-s relationKind=ASSOCIATION` fails with `must be aggregation if transient`. A transient relation to an unmapped target with a defined form renders as a nested inline form (inline create), not as a picker; a picker is used for a transient relation to a mapped reference transfer object.

heading: Practice > Practice notes: pick a customization level per actor
replaces: - The pattern extends to three or more actors; some can be dashboard-only placeholders. Actors can differ in authentication (for example an anonymous public actor next to authenticated staff actors).
proposed: - Two actors are the tested shape. A third actor breaks the generated admin frontend build (known issue): `./judo.sh build` stops at `pnpm run format` (biome) with `Declarations inside of a import declaration may not have duplicates`, for example `import type { CsvFile, CsvFile, CsvFileStored, CsvFileStored }`, when an operation has an input and an output of the same type. The template emits one import per entry of `getApiImportsForPage`, and that list is built from a `HashSet<ClassType>` that deduplicates by object identity, so two ClassType objects for one class produce duplicate lines. Present with any third actor (human or system, anonymous or not, with or without an access) and gone when the third actor is removed. Workaround: keep the frontend to two actors and route the extra operation through an existing actor (for example a technical admin call); do not add a third actor to a module that has such operations.

heading: Mandatory rules
replaces: 3. **Always paginate query results.** Use `limit`, `offset`, and `totalCount` together. Without explicit pagination, large result sets are silently truncated and the assistant operates on a partial view of the model.
proposed: 3. **Always paginate query results.** Use `limit`, `offset`, and `totalCount` together. `query` and `graphql` apply `limit` only when it is given, so without it every match is returned and nothing is truncated by the CLI. Helper scripts that pass a fixed `--limit` (for example `--limit 800`) do truncate silently, so check `totalCount` against the number of items returned.
